---
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
Fix a set $\symbf{Prop}$ of \emph{propositional variables}. We define modal formulas $\varphi$ inductively as follows: 
    \[
        \varphi ::= p \mid \top \mid \neg \varphi \mid \varphi \to \varphi \mid \symbol{"25A1} \varphi,
    \]
    where $p \in \symbf{Prop}$. We write $\mathbf{MF}$ for the set of modal formulas.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
A \emph{closure frame} $\symcal{F}$ is a tuple $(W, G, \mathrm{cl})$ where:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $W$ is a non-empty set of \emph{possible worlds}.
        \item $G: W \to \symcal{P}(\mathbf{MF})$ is a \emph{generator}.
        \item $\mathrm{cl}: \symcal{P}(\mathbf{MF}) \to \symcal{P}(\mathbf{MF})$ is a \emph{closure}.
    \end{itemize}
    A closure model $\symcal{M}$ is a tuple $(\symcal{F}, V)$ where $\symcal{F}$ is a closure frame and $V: \symbf{Prop} \to \symcal{P}(W)$ is a \emph{valuation function}.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
Given a closure model $\symcal{M}$, a world $w \in \symcal{M}$, and $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$, we define $\symcal{M}, w \models \varphi$ as follows:
    \begin{align*}
        \symcal{M}, w \models \top &\text{ always} \\
        \symcal{M}, w \models p &\iff w \in V(p) \text{ where } p \in \symbf{Prop} \\
        \symcal{M}, w \models \neg \varphi &\iff \text{not } \symcal{M}, w \models \varphi \ (\symcal{M}, w \nvDash \varphi) \\
        \symcal{M}, w \models \varphi \to \psi &\iff \symcal{M}, w \nvDash \varphi \text{ or } \symcal{M}, w \models \psi \\
        \symcal{M}, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \varphi &\iff \varphi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w)).
    \end{align*}
    If $\symcal{M}$ under consideration is clear from the context, we simply write $w \models \varphi$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
We define the following notions of validity and semantic consequence. Here, $\varphi$ is a modal formula and $\Gamma$ is a set of formulas:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item A formula $\varphi$ is \emph{valid in a model $\symcal{M}$}, denoted by $\symcal{M} \models \varphi$, if $\symcal{M}, w \models \varphi$ for all $w \in \symcal{M}$. Moreover, a formula $\varphi$ is \emph{valid in a frame $\symcal{F}$}, denoted by $\symcal{F} \models \varphi$, if $(\symcal{F}, V), w \models \varphi$ for all $V$ and $w \in \symcal{F}$.
        \item A formula $\varphi$ is \emph{valid}, denoted by $\models \varphi$, if $\symcal{M}, w \models \varphi$ for all $\symcal{M}$ and $w \in \symcal{M}$. 
        \item \emph{A set $\Gamma$ semantically entails $\varphi$}, denoted by $\Gamma \models \varphi$, if for all $\symcal{M}$ and $w \in \symcal{M}$, $\symcal{M}, w \models \Gamma$ implies $\symcal{M}, w \models \varphi$.
        \item Given a class $\mathbb{C}$ of closure frames, \emph{$\Gamma$ semantically entails $\varphi$ over $\mathbb{C}$}, denoted by $\Gamma \models_{\mathbb{C}} \varphi$, if for any $\symcal{F} \in \mathbb{C}$, $V$, and $w \in \symcal{F}$ $(\symcal{F}, V), w \models \Gamma$ implies $(\symcal{F}, V), w \models \varphi$.
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
We define the properties \textsf{(E)}, \textsf{(G)}, \textsf{(M)}, \textsf{(C)}, \textsf{(N)}, \textsf{(K)} of closure frames in Figure \ref{fig:property-closure-frame}.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
Let $\symcal{F}$ be a closure frame. Then, the following statements hold:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item $\symcal{F}$ satisfies \textsf{(E)} if and only if $\mathsf{Log}(\symcal{F})$ is closed under \textsf{RE}.
        \item $\symcal{F}$ satisfies \textsf{(G)} if and only if $\mathsf{Log}(\symcal{F})$ is closed under \textsf{Gen}.
        \item For each $\mathsf{X} \in \{ \mathsf{M}, \mathsf{C}, \mathsf{N}, \mathsf{K} \}$, $\symcal{F}$ satisfies \textsf{(X)} if and only if $\mathsf{X} \in \mathsf{Log}(\symcal{F})$.
    \end{enumerate}
    \label{prop:correspondence}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
We prove only the cases for \textsf{(E)} and \textsf{(M)}. The other cases are proved similarly.

    Suppose first that $\symcal{F}$ satisfies \textsf{(E)}, and assume that $\symcal{F} \models \varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$.
    Then, for every $w \in \symcal{F}$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$ if and only if $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$ by \textsf{(E)}.
    Hence, for every valuation $V$ and every $w \in \symcal{F}$,
    \[
        (\symcal{F}, V), w \models \symbol{"25A1} \varphi \iff (\symcal{F}, V), w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi.
    \]
    Therefore, $\symcal{F} \models \symbol{"25A1} \varphi \leftrightarrow \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.

    Conversely, suppose that $\mathsf{Log}(\symcal{F})$ is closed under \textsf{RE}, and assume that $\symcal{F} \models \varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$.
    From the latter, we have $\varphi \leftrightarrow \psi \in \mathsf{Log}(\symcal{F})$, and hence $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi \leftrightarrow \symbol{"25A1} \psi \in \mathsf{Log}(\symcal{F})$ by \textsf{RE}.
    Therefore, for every $w \in \symcal{F}$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$ if and only if $\psi\in\mathrm{cl}(G(w))$.

    Next, suppose that $\symcal{F}$ satisfies \textsf{(M)}.
    Let $V$ be any valuation and $w \in \symcal{F}$, and suppose that $(\symcal{F}, V), w \models \symbol{"25A1} (\varphi \land \psi)$.
    Then, $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$ holds.
    By \textsf{(M)}, we have $\varphi, \psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$, and hence
    $(\symcal{F}, V), w \models \symbol{"25A1} \varphi \land \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.

    Conversely, suppose that $\mathsf{M} \in \mathsf{Log}(\symcal{F})$.
    Take any $w \in \symcal{F}$, and suppose that $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$.
    In this situation, we have $(\symcal{F}, V), w \models \symbol{"25A1} (\varphi \land \psi)$ for any valuation $V$. Then, it follows that $(\symcal{F}, V), w \models \symbol{"25A1} \varphi \land \symbol{"25A1} \psi$ by \textsf{M}.
    Therefore, $\varphi, \psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
A \emph{modal logic} $L$ is a subset of $\mathbf{MF}$ that contains all classical tautologies and is closed under \textit{modus ponens} and uniform substitution. We say that a formula $\varphi$ is \emph{provable} in a logic $L$ from $\Gamma$ if there are formulas $\gamma_1, \ldots, \gamma_n \in \Gamma$ such that $\gamma_1 \land \cdots \land \gamma_n \to \varphi \in L$\footnote{We allow $n = 0$, in which case the empty conjunction is understood as $\top$.}.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
For $\Lambda \subseteq \{ \mathsf{E, G, M, C, N, K} \}$, we define $L_\Lambda$ as the smallest modal logic satisfying the following conditions:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $L_\Lambda$ is closed under \textsf{RE} if $\mathsf{E} \in \Lambda$.
        \item $L_\Lambda$ is closed under \textsf{Gen} if $\mathsf{G} \in \Lambda$.
        \item For each $\mathsf{X} \in \{ \mathsf{M, C, N, K} \}$, $L_\Lambda$ contains an axiom scheme\textsf{X} if $\mathsf{X} \in \Lambda$.
    \end{itemize}
    We write $\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \varphi$ to mean that $\varphi$ is provable in $L_\Lambda$ from $\Gamma$.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
Let $\Lambda \subseteq \{ \mathsf{E, G, M, C, N, K} \}$. Then, the logic $L_\Lambda$ is sound with respect to the class $\mathbf{CF}_\Lambda$ of frames. That is, $\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \varphi$ implies $\Gamma \models_\Lambda \varphi$.
    \label{thm:soundness-closure-frame}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
The modal logics $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{N}$ are incomparable; that is, neither $\mathbf{E} \subseteq \mathbf{N}$ nor $\mathbf{N} \subseteq \mathbf{E}$ holds.
\label{prop:E-N-incomparable}
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By Theorem \ref{thm:soundness-closure-frame}, it suffices to construct a closure model whose underlying frame satisfies \textsf{(G)} in which some theorem of $\mathbf{E}$ is false, and a closure model whose underlying frame satisfies \textsf{(E)} in which some theorem of $\mathbf{N}$ is false.

For the first direction, let $\symcal{M}_1 = (\{w\}, G, \mathrm{id}, V)$ be a closure model such that $G(w) = \mathbf{MF} \setminus \{p\}$.
Then, its underlying frame satisfies \textsf{(G)}; indeed, the only formula not belonging to $G(w)$ is $p$, which is not valid on the frame.
Since $p\leftrightarrow\neg\neg p$ is a classical tautology,
$\symbol{"25A1} p \leftrightarrow \symbol{"25A1} \neg \neg p \in \mathbf{E}$.
However, $\symcal{M}_1, w \nvDash \symbol{"25A1} p$ and $\symcal{M}_1, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \neg \neg p$.
Therefore, $\mathbf{E} \nsubseteq \mathbf{N}$.

For the converse direction, let $\symcal{M}_2 = (\{w\}, G, \mathrm{id}, V)$ be a closure model such that $G(w) = \emptyset$.
Its underlying frame satisfies \textsf{(E)} trivially.
Since $\top \in \mathbf{N}$, we have $\symbol{"25A1} \top \in \mathbf{N}$ by \textsf{Gen}.
However, $\symcal{M}_2, w \nvDash \symbol{"25A1} \top$.
Therefore, $\mathbf{N}\nsubseteq\mathbf{E}$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
Let $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$. We define $\mathsf{Sub}(\varphi)$ as the set of all subformulas of $\varphi$. Moreover, we define some sets of formulas as follows:
    \begin{align*}
        \mathsf{Sub}^\symbol{"25A1} (\varphi) &= \mathsf{Sub}(\varphi) \cup \{ \symbol{"25A1} \psi \mid \psi \in \mathsf{Sub}(\varphi) \} \cup \{ \top, \symbol{"25A1} \top \} \\
        \mathsf{Sub}^* (\varphi) &= \mathsf{Sub}^\symbol{"25A1} (\varphi) \cup \{ \sim \psi \mid \psi \in \mathsf{Sub}^\symbol{"25A1} (\varphi) \}.
    \end{align*}
    Here, $\sim \psi$ denotes $\chi$ if $\psi$ is of the form $\neg \chi$, and denotes $\neg \psi$ otherwise.

    We also define $\mathsf{Sub}(\Gamma)$ for a set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas as the union of $\mathsf{Sub}(\gamma)$ for every $\gamma \in \Gamma$. The sets $\mathsf{Sub}^\symbol{"25A1}(\Gamma)$ and $\mathsf{Sub}^*(\Gamma)$ are defined likewise.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
Let $\Gamma, \Delta$ be sets of modal formulas.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\Gamma$ is \emph{$L_\Lambda$-consistent} if $\Gamma \nvdash_\Lambda \bot$.
        \item $\Gamma$ is \emph{maximally $L_\Lambda$-consistent} if $\Gamma$ is $L_\Lambda$-consistent and $\psi \in \Gamma$ or $\sim \psi \in \Gamma$ for all $\psi \in \mathbf{MF}$.
        \item $\Gamma$ is \emph{$\mathsf{Sub}^*(\Delta)$-maximally $L_\Lambda$-consistent} if $\Gamma$ is $L_\Lambda$-consistent and $\psi \in \Gamma$ or $\sim \psi \in \Gamma$ for all $\psi \in \mathsf{Sub}^*(\Delta)$.
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
We define $\mathrm{cl}_\Lambda$. First, for a given set $\Gamma$ of formulas, we define a sequence $(\Gamma^\Lambda_n)_{n \in \omega}$ of sets as follows:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
        \item $\Gamma^\Lambda_0 = \Gamma \cup \{ \top \}$ if $\mathsf{N} \in \Lambda$, and $\Gamma^\Lambda_0 = \Gamma$ otherwise.
        \item $\Gamma^\Lambda_{n+1}$ is the union of $\Gamma^\Lambda_n$ and the following sets:
        \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
            \item $\{ \psi, \chi \mid \psi \land \chi \in \Gamma^\Lambda_n \}$ if $\mathsf{M} \in \Lambda$ \label{closure-construction-case-m}
            \item $\{ \psi \land \chi \mid \psi, \chi \in \Gamma^\Lambda_n \}$ if $\mathsf{C} \in \Lambda$ \label{closure-construction-case-c}
            \item $\{ \chi \mid \psi, \psi \to \chi \in \Gamma^\Lambda_n \}$ if $\mathsf{K} \in \Lambda$. \label{closure-construction-case-k}
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
    Then, we define $\mathrm{cl}_\Lambda$ as $\mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(\Gamma) = \bigcup_{n \in \omega} \Gamma^\Lambda_n$.
    \label{def:closure-onepoint}
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
Given an $L_\Lambda$-consistent set $\Gamma$ of formulas, we define $\symcal{M}^\Gamma_\Lambda = (W, G, \mathrm{cl}, V)$ as follows:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $W$ is a singleton $\{ \Delta_\Gamma \}$, where $\Delta_\Gamma$ is a $\mathsf{Sub}^*(\Gamma)$-maximally $L_\Lambda$-consistent set satisfying $\Gamma \subseteq \Delta_\Gamma \subseteq \mathsf{Sub}^*(\Gamma)$.
        \item $G(\Delta_\Gamma) = \{ \varphi \in \mathsf{Sub}^*(\Gamma) \mid \symbol{"25A1} \varphi \in \Delta_\Gamma \}$.
        \item $\mathrm{cl} = \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda$ defined in Definition \ref{def:closure-onepoint}.
        \item $V(p) = \{ \Delta_\Gamma \}$ if $p \in \Delta_\Gamma$, and $V(p) = \emptyset$ otherwise.
    \end{itemize}
    \label{def:countermodel-onepoint}
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
For any $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi \in \mathsf{Sub}^*(\Gamma)$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Delta_\Gamma))$ implies $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi \in \Delta_\Gamma$.
    \label{lem:reflection-onepoint}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
We show the following claim by induction on $n$:
    \begin{center}
        \textbf{Claim.} for any $\varphi$, $\varphi \in (G(\Delta_\Gamma))^\Lambda_n$ implies $\Delta_\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \symbol{"25A1} \varphi$.
    \end{center}
    \begin{proof}[Proof of the Claim.]
        In the base case $n = 0$, it is straightforward from the definition of $G(\Delta_\Gamma)$, except when $\varphi = \top$ and $\top \notin G(\Delta_\Gamma)$. In this case, $\top$ is added to $(G(\Delta_\Gamma))^\Lambda_0$ because $\mathsf{N} \in \Lambda$. Hence, $\Delta_\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \symbol{"25A1} \top$ follows from axiom \textsf{N}.
    
        For the inductive step, suppose that the claim holds for $n \leq k$ and $\varphi \in (G(\Delta_\Gamma))^\Lambda_{k+1}$.
        If $\varphi \in (G(\Delta_\Gamma))^\Lambda_k$, the claim follows immediately from the induction hypothesis.
    
        Suppose that $\varphi$ is added by clause \ref{closure-construction-case-m}, so that $\varphi \land \psi \in (G(\Delta_\Gamma))^\Lambda_k$ for some $\psi$.
        By the induction hypothesis, $\Delta_\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \symbol{"25A1}(\varphi \land \psi)$.
        Hence, $\Delta_\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \symbol{"25A1}\varphi$ by the axiom scheme \textsf{M}.
        The cases for clauses \ref{closure-construction-case-c} and \ref{closure-construction-case-k} are proved similarly, using the axiom schemata \textsf{C} and \textsf{K}, respectively.
    \end{proof}
    Finally, suppose that $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi \in \mathsf{Sub}^*(\Gamma)$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Delta_\Gamma))$. Then, the claim yields that $\Delta_\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \symbol{"25A1} \varphi$. Since $\Delta_\Gamma$ is $\mathsf{Sub}^*(\Gamma)$-maximally $L_\Lambda$-consistent, we have $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi \in \Delta_\Gamma$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
In the base case $n = 0$, it is straightforward from the definition of $G(\Delta_\Gamma)$, except when $\varphi = \top$ and $\top \notin G(\Delta_\Gamma)$. In this case, $\top$ is added to $(G(\Delta_\Gamma))^\Lambda_0$ because $\mathsf{N} \in \Lambda$. Hence, $\Delta_\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \symbol{"25A1} \top$ follows from axiom \textsf{N}.
    
        For the inductive step, suppose that the claim holds for $n \leq k$ and $\varphi \in (G(\Delta_\Gamma))^\Lambda_{k+1}$.
        If $\varphi \in (G(\Delta_\Gamma))^\Lambda_k$, the claim follows immediately from the induction hypothesis.
    
        Suppose that $\varphi$ is added by clause \ref{closure-construction-case-m}, so that $\varphi \land \psi \in (G(\Delta_\Gamma))^\Lambda_k$ for some $\psi$.
        By the induction hypothesis, $\Delta_\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \symbol{"25A1}(\varphi \land \psi)$.
        Hence, $\Delta_\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \symbol{"25A1}\varphi$ by the axiom scheme \textsf{M}.
        The cases for clauses \ref{closure-construction-case-c} and \ref{closure-construction-case-k} are proved similarly, using the axiom schemata \textsf{C} and \textsf{K}, respectively.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
For any $\varphi \in \mathsf{Sub}^*(\Gamma)$, $\symcal{M}_\Lambda^\Gamma, \Delta_\Gamma \models \varphi$ if and only if $\varphi \in \Delta_\Gamma$.
    \label{lem:truth-lemma-onepoint}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
By induction on the complexity of $\varphi$.
    Since the base case and the inductive cases for the Boolean connectives are straightforward, we only show the case $\varphi = \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.

    If $\Delta_\Gamma \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi$, then $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Delta_\Gamma))$ by the satisfaction clause for $\symbol{"25A1}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:reflection-onepoint}, $\symbol{"25A1} \psi \in \Delta_\Gamma$. Conversely, if $\symbol{"25A1} \psi \in \Delta_\Gamma$, then $\psi \in G(\Delta_\Gamma) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Delta_\Gamma))$. Therefore, we have $\Delta_\Gamma \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
The model $\symcal{M}_\Lambda^\Gamma$ satisfies the property \textsf{(X)} if $\mathsf{X} \in \Lambda$.
    \label{lem:corresponding-lemma-onepoint}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
If $\mathsf{N} \in \Lambda$, then $\top \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Delta_\Gamma))$ is straightforward from the construction of $\mathrm{cl}_\Lambda$. 
    
    Suppose that $\mathsf{M} \in \Lambda$ and $\varphi \land \psi \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Delta_\Gamma))$.
    Then, by clause \ref{closure-construction-case-m} of Definition \ref{def:closure-onepoint}, we have $\varphi, \psi \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Delta_\Gamma))$. We can prove the cases for \textsf{C} and \textsf{K} similarly.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
Let $\Lambda \subseteq \{ \mathsf{M, C, N, K} \}$. Then, the logic $L_\Lambda$ is strongly complete with respect to the class $\mathbf{CF}_\Lambda$ of frames. That is, $\Gamma \models_\Lambda \varphi$ implies $\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \varphi$.
    \label{thm:completeness-onepoint}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Suppose that $\Gamma \nvdash_\Lambda \varphi$. Then, the set $\Sigma = \Gamma \cup \{ \neg \varphi \}$ is $L_\Lambda$-consistent. By Lindenbaum's Lemma, we can make a $\mathsf{Sub}^*(\Sigma)$-maximally $L_\Lambda$-consistent set $\Delta_\Sigma$ such that $\Gamma \cup \{ \neg \varphi \} \subseteq \Delta_\Sigma$. Then, by Lemma \ref{lem:truth-lemma-onepoint}, we have a model $\symcal{M}_\Lambda^\Sigma$ and its world $\Delta_\Sigma$ such that $\Delta_\Sigma \models \Gamma$ and $\Delta_\Sigma \nvDash \varphi$. Moreover, $\symcal{M}_\Lambda^\Sigma$ satisfies all properties \textsf{(X)} such that $\mathsf{X} \in \Lambda$ by Lemma \ref{lem:corresponding-lemma-onepoint}. Therefore, we have $\Gamma \nvDash_\Lambda \varphi$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
Let $\Lambda \subseteq \{ \mathsf{M, C, N, K} \}$. Then, $L_\Lambda$ has the finite model property.
    \label{cor:fmp}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Suppose that $\nvdash_\Lambda \varphi$. In Definition \ref{def:countermodel-onepoint}, assume that $\Gamma = \{ \neg \varphi \}$.
    Then, the model $\symcal{M}^\Gamma_\Lambda$ is a countermodel for $\varphi$.
    Moreover, $W$ is finite and $G(\Delta_\Gamma)$ is also finite since $\mathsf{Sub}^*(\neg \varphi)$ is finite.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
Let $\Lambda \subseteq \{ \mathsf{M, C, N, K} \}$. Then $L_\Lambda$ is decidable.
    In fact, $L_\Lambda$ is primitive recursive.
    \label{cor:decidability}
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Fix a modal formula $\varphi$.
    Since $\mathsf{Sub}^*(\neg \varphi)$ is finite, there are only finitely many subsets $\Delta \subseteq \mathsf{Sub}^*(\neg \varphi)$.
    For each such $\Delta$, we construct the one-point model $\symcal{M} = (W, G, \mathrm{cl}, V)$ as follows:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $W = \{ \Delta \}$
        \item $G(\Delta) = \{ \psi \in \mathsf{Sub}^*(\neg \varphi) \mid \symbol{"25A1} \psi \in \Delta \}$
        \item $\mathrm{cl} = \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda$
        \item $V(p) = \{ \Delta \}$ if $p \in \Delta$, and $V(p) = \emptyset$ otherwise.
    \end{itemize}
    These are finite models, and by the definition of $\mathrm{cl}_\Lambda$, each such model satisfies all the conditions \textsf{(X)} with $\mathsf{X} \in \Lambda$. Moreover, the relation $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Delta))$ is primitive recursive.
    Indeed, for a fixed $\psi$, it suffices to perform the construction of Definition \ref{def:closure-onepoint} within the finite set of subformulas of $G(\Delta)\cup\{\psi,\top\}$.
    This restricted construction stabilizes after a primitively recursively bounded number of stages, and each stage is primitive recursive.
    Hence, for each candidate model, whether $\neg \varphi$ is true in it can be determined in finite time.
    
    If $\nvdash_\Lambda \varphi$, the countermodel constructed in Corollary \ref{cor:fmp} yields one of these candidates in which $\varphi$ is false.
    Conversely, if one of these candidates falsifies $\varphi$, then $\nvdash_\Lambda \varphi$ by soundness.
    Therefore, $\vdash_\Lambda \varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is true in all of the finitely many candidates above.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
We define $\mathrm{cl}_\Lambda$ for $\Lambda \subseteq \{ \mathsf{E, G, M, C, N, K} \}$. First, for a given set $\Gamma$ of formulas, we define a sequence $(\Gamma^\Lambda_n)_{n \in \omega}$ of sets as follows:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
        \item $\Gamma^\Lambda_0$ is the union of $\Gamma$ and the following sets:
        \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
            \item $L_\Lambda$ if $\mathsf{G} \in \Lambda$
            \item $\{ \top \}$ if $\mathsf{N} \in \Lambda$.
        \end{enumerate}
        \item $\Gamma^\Lambda_{n+1}$ is defined in the same way as in Definition \ref{def:closure-onepoint}.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then, we define $\mathrm{cl}_\Lambda$ as $\mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(\Gamma) = \bigcup_{n \in \omega} \Gamma^\Lambda_n$.
    \label{def:closure-full}
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
We define $\symcal{M}_\Lambda = (W, G, \mathrm{cl}, V)$ as follows:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $W$ is the set of all maximally $L_\Lambda$-consistent sets.
        \item $G(\Gamma) = \{ \varphi \in \mathbf{MF} \mid \symbol{"25A1} \varphi \in \Gamma \}$.
        \item $\mathrm{cl} = \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda$ defined in Definition \ref{def:closure-full}.
        \item $V(p) = \{ \Gamma \mid p \in \Gamma \}$.
    \end{itemize}
    \label{def:countermodel-full}
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
For any $\Gamma \in W$ and $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$, if $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(\Gamma))$, then $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi \in \Gamma$.
    \label{lem:reflection-full}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
The proof proceeds as in Lemma \ref{lem:reflection-onepoint}.
    
    The only additional case is that $\varphi \in (G(\Gamma))^\Lambda_0$ because $\varphi \in L_\Lambda$.
    In this case, we have $\mathsf{G} \in \Lambda$, so $\symbol{"25A1}\varphi \in L_\Lambda$ by \textsf{Gen}, and hence $\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \symbol{"25A1}\varphi$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
For any $\Gamma \in W$ and any $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$, $\symcal{M}_\Lambda, \Gamma \models \varphi$ if and only if $\varphi \in \Gamma$.
    \label{lem:truth-lemma-full}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
By induction on the complexity of $\varphi$.
    Particularly, the case $\varphi = \symbol{"25A1} \psi$ is proved as in Lemma \ref{lem:truth-lemma-onepoint}, using Lemma \ref{lem:reflection-full}.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
The model $\symcal{M}_\Lambda$ satisfies the property \textsf{(X)} if $\mathsf{X} \in \Lambda$.
    \label{lem:corresponding-lemma-full}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
We only prove the cases $\mathsf{E} \in \Lambda$ and $\mathsf{G} \in \Lambda$.
    The other cases are proved as in Lemma \ref{lem:corresponding-lemma-onepoint}. 
    Let $\symcal{F}_\Lambda$ be the underlying frame of $\symcal{M}_\Lambda$.

    To prove the case $\mathsf{E} \in \Lambda$, suppose $\symcal{F}_\Lambda \models \varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$. In particular, we have $\symcal{M}_\Lambda \models \varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$. This means that $\Gamma \models \varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$ for all $\Gamma \in W$, and that is equivalent to $\varphi \leftrightarrow \psi \in \Gamma$. Since $\bigcap_{\Gamma \in W} \Gamma = L_\Lambda$, we have $\varphi \leftrightarrow \psi \in L_\Lambda$. By \textsf{RE}, $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi \leftrightarrow \symbol{"25A1} \psi \in L_\Lambda$. Thus, $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi \in \Gamma$ is equivalent to $\symbol{"25A1} \psi \in \Gamma$. By the definition of $G$ and Lemma \ref{lem:reflection-full}, we have $\chi \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Gamma))$ if and only if $\symbol{"25A1} \chi \in \Gamma$ for all $\chi \in \mathbf{MF}$, and hence $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Gamma))$ if and only if $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Gamma))$.

    Suppose now that $\mathsf{G} \in \Lambda$, suppose $\symcal{F}_\Lambda \models \varphi$, which implies we have $\symcal{M}_\Lambda \models \varphi$. By the same argument as the previous case, we have $\varphi \in L_\Lambda$. By \textsf{Gen}, $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi \in L_\Lambda$. Since $L_\Lambda \subseteq \Gamma$ for any $\Gamma$, we have $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi \in \Gamma$. By the definition of $G$, we have $\varphi \in G(\Gamma)$, which yields $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}_\Lambda(G(\Gamma))$ as in the previous case.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
Let $\Lambda \subseteq \{ \mathsf{E, G, M, C, N, K} \}$. Then, the logic $L_\Lambda$ is strongly complete with respect to the class $\mathbf{CF}_\Lambda$ of frames. That is, $\Gamma \models_\Lambda \varphi$ implies $\Gamma \vdash_\Lambda \varphi$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Similar argument as that for Theorem \ref{thm:completeness-onepoint}, using Lemmas \ref{lem:truth-lemma-full} and \ref{lem:corresponding-lemma-full}.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
Let $\Lambda \subseteq \{ \mathsf{E, G, M, C, N, K} \}$ and $\Lambda' \subseteq \{ \mathsf{E_{\symcal{M}}, G_{\symcal{M}}, M, C, N, K} \}$ such that $\mathsf{E} \in \Lambda$ if and only if $\mathsf{E_{\symcal{M}}} \in \Lambda'$, $\mathsf{G} \in \Lambda$ if and only if $\mathsf{G_{\symcal{M}}} \in \Lambda'$, and $\Lambda \cap \{ \mathsf{M, C, N, K} \} = \Lambda' \cap \{ \mathsf{M, C, N, K} \}$. Then,
\[
    \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{CM}_{\Lambda}) =
    \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{CM}_{\Lambda'}) = L_{\Lambda}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
By soundness and completeness, we have $\mathsf{Log}(\mathrm{CM}_\Lambda) = L_\Lambda$.
Moreover, the canonical model constructed in Definition \ref{def:countermodel-full} satisfies $(\mathsf{E}_{\symcal{M}})$ whenever $\mathsf{E} \in \Lambda$ and $(\mathsf{G}_{\symcal{M}})$ whenever $\mathsf{G} \in \Lambda$ by the same argument as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:corresponding-lemma-full}.
Hence, if $\varphi\notin L_\Lambda$, this canonical model belongs to $\mathrm{CM}_{\Lambda'}$ and falsifies $\varphi$.
Together with soundness, this yields $\mathsf{Log}(\mathrm{CM}_{\Lambda'})=L_\Lambda$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
A \emph{neighborhood frame} is a tuple $\symcal{F}_N = (W, N)$ where $W$ is a non-empty set and $N$ is a function $N: W \to \symcal{P}(\symcal{P}(W))$. A \emph{neighborhood model} is a tuple $\symcal{M}_N = (W, N, V)$ where $(W, N)$ is a neighborhood frame and $V$ is a valuation function $V: \symbf{Prop} \to \symcal{P}(W)$.
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
The relation $\symcal{M}_N, w \models \varphi$ is defined as for closure models, except for the modal operator, which is defined as follows:
    \[
        \symcal{M}_N, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \varphi \iff \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_N} \in N(w).
    \]
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
Given a neighborhood model $\symcal{M}_N = (W, N, V)$, we define $f_N(\symcal{M}_N) = (W, G^{f_N}, \mathrm{id}, V)$ where
    \[
        G^{f_N}(w) = \{ \varphi \in \mathbf{MF} \mid \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_N} \in N(w) \}.
    \]
    \label{def:neighborhood-to-closure-function}
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
Let $\symcal{M}_N$ be a neighborhood model. Then, for any $w \in \symcal{M}_N$ and $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$, $\symcal{M}_N, w \models \varphi$ if and only if $f_N(\symcal{M}_N), w \models \varphi$.
    \label{lem:neighborhood-to-closure-preserving}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
By induction on the complexity of $\varphi$. The atomic case is immediate because $f_N$ preserves the valuation. The Boolean cases are straightforward. Thus, it remains only to consider the case $\varphi = \symbol{"25A1} \psi$, which is proven as follows:
    \begin{align*}
        \symcal{M}_N, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi &\iff \lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_N} \in N(w) \\
        &\iff \psi \in G^{f_N}(w) \\
        &\iff \psi \in \mathrm{id}(G^{f_N}(w)) \\
        &\iff f_N(\symcal{M}_N), w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi. \qedhere
    \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
For any neighborhood model $\symcal{M}_N$, the model $f_N(\symcal{M}_N)$ has the property \textsf{(E)}.
    \label{lem:neighborhood-has-E}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Suppose that $f_N(\symcal{M}_N) \models \varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$.
    \begin{align*}
        f_N(\symcal{M}_N) \models \varphi \leftrightarrow \psi &\iff \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{f_N(\symcal{M}_N)} = \lBrack \psi \rBrack_{f_N(\symcal{M}_N)} & \\
        &\iff \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_N} = \lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_N} &\text{Lemma \ref{lem:neighborhood-to-closure-preserving}} \\
        &\implies (\varphi \in G_{f_N}(w) \iff \psi \in G_{f_N}(w)) & \\
        &\iff (\varphi \in \mathrm{id}(G^{f_N}(w)) \iff \psi \in \mathrm{id}(G^{f_N}(w))). & \qedhere
    \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
Given a closure model $\symcal{M} = (W, G, \mathrm{cl}, V)$, we define $g_N(\symcal{M}) = (W, N^{g_N}, V)$ where
    \[
        N^{g_N}(w) = \{ \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} \mid \varphi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w)) \}.
    \]
    \label{def:closure-to-neighborhood-function}
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
Suppose that $\symcal{M}$ satisfies \textsf{(E)}. Then, for any $w \in \symcal{M}$ and $\varphi, \psi \in \mathbf{MF}$, $\lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} = \lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}$ implies that $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$ if and only if $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$.
    \label{lem:truthset-to-closure-by-E}
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
If $\lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} = \lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}$, then $w \models \varphi$ and $w \models \psi$ are equivalent for all $w \in \symcal{M}$. This means that $w \models \varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$ for all $w$. Hence, $\symcal{M} \models \varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$. Therefore, by \textsf{(E)}, $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$ if and only if $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
Let $\symcal{M}$ be a closure model that satisfies \textsf{(E)}. Then, for any $w \in \symcal{M}$ and $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$, $\symcal{M}, w \models \varphi$ if and only if $g_N(\symcal{M}), w \models \varphi$.
    \label{lem:closure-to-neighborhood-preserving}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
By induction on the complexity of $\varphi$.
    We only prove the case $\varphi = \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.
    First, we show the left-to-right direction.
    If $\symcal{M}, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi$, then $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$.
    By definition of $N^{g_N}$, $\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} \in N^{g_N}(w)$, which is equivalent to $\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{g_N(\symcal{M})} \in N^{g_N}(w)$ by the induction hypothesis. Therefore, we have $g_N(\symcal{M}), w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.

    Conversely, suppose that $g_N(\symcal{M}), w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi$. Then, $\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{g_N(\symcal{M})} \in N^{g_N}(w)$, which means $\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} \in N^{g_N}(w)$ by the induction hypothesis. Thus, we have a formula $\chi$ such that $\chi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$ and $\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} = \lBrack \chi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:truthset-to-closure-by-E}, we have $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$, which means $\symcal{M}, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
The translations $f_N: \mathbf{NM} \to \mathbf{CM}_\mathsf{E}$ and $g_N: \mathbf{CM}_\mathsf{E} \to \mathbf{NM}$ are truth-preserving.
\label{thm:neighborhood-closure-representation}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\[
        \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{NM}) = \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{CM_\mathsf{E}}).
    \]
    \label{cor:neighborhood-closure-equivalence}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
An \emph{FMT frame} is a tuple $\symcal{F}_F = (W, \{R_\varphi\}_{\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}})$ where $W$ is a non-empty set and $R_\varphi \subseteq W \times W$ is a binary relation for each $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$.
    
    An \emph{FMT model} is a tuple $\symcal{M}_F = (W, \{R_\varphi\}_{\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}}, V)$ where $(W, \{R_\varphi\}_{\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}})$ is an FMT frame and $V$ is a valuation function $V: \symbf{Prop} \to \symcal{P}(W)$.
    \label{def:FMT model}
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
The relation $\symcal{M}_F, w \models \varphi$ is defined as for closure models, except for the modal operator, which is defined as follows:
    \[
        \symcal{M}_F, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \varphi
        \iff
        \text{for every } v \in W,\ w R_\varphi v \text{ implies } \symcal{M}_F, v \models \varphi.
    \]
    \label{def:FMT-satisfaction}
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- definition-20: body_md -->
Given an FMT model $\symcal{M}_F = (W, \{R_\varphi\}_{\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}}, V)$, we define $f_F(\symcal{M}_F) = (W, G^{f_F}, \mathrm{id}, V)$ where
    \[
        G^{f_F}(w)
        =
        \{ \varphi \in \mathbf{MF} \mid
        R_\varphi[w]
        \subseteq \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_F} \}.
    \]
    Here, $R_\varphi[w]$ denotes the set $\{v \in W \mid w R_\varphi v\}$.
    \label{def:FMT-to-closure-function}
<!-- end definition-20 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
Let $\symcal{M}_F$ be an FMT model. Then, for any $w \in \symcal{M}_F$ and $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$, $\symcal{M}_F, w \models \varphi$ if and only if $f_F(\symcal{M}_F), w \models \varphi$.
    \label{lem:FMT-to-closure-preserving}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
By induction on the complexity of $\varphi$.
    The atomic case and the Boolean cases are straightforward, so we consider only the modal case $\varphi = \symbol{"25A1} \psi$:
    \begin{align*}
        \symcal{M}_F, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi
        &\iff  (w R_\psi v \implies \symcal{M}_F, v \models \psi) \text{ for all } v \in W \\
        &\iff \psi \in G^{f_F}(w) \\
        &\iff \psi \in \mathrm{id}(G^{f_F}(w)) \\
        &\iff f_F(\symcal{M}_F), w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi. \qedhere
    \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
For any FMT model $\symcal{M}_F$, the model $f_F(\symcal{M}_F)$ has the property \textsf{(G)}.
    \label{lem:FMT-has-G}
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Suppose that $f_F(\symcal{M}_F) \models \varphi$. By Lemma \ref{lem:FMT-to-closure-preserving}, $\symcal{M}_F \models \varphi$, and hence $\lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_F}=W$. Then, for every $w \in W$,
    \[
        \{v \in W \mid wR_\varphi v\}
        \subseteq
        \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_F}.
    \]
    Thus, $\varphi \in G^{f_F}(w)=\mathrm{id}(G^{f_F}(w))$ for every $w \in W$. Therefore, $f_F(\symcal{M}_F)$ has the property \textsf{(G)}.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- definition-21: body_md -->
Given a closure model $\symcal{M} = (W, G, \mathrm{cl}, V)$, we define $g_F(\symcal{M}) = (W, \{R^{g_F}_\varphi\}_{\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}}, V)$ where:
    \[
    R_\varphi^{g_F}[w] =
        \begin{cases}
            W \setminus \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} &\text{if } \varphi \notin \mathrm{cl}(G(w)) \\
            \emptyset &\text{otherwise.}
        \end{cases}
    \]
    \label{def:closure-to-FMT-function}
<!-- end definition-21 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
Let $\symcal{M}$ be a closure model that satisfies \textsf{(G)}. Then, for any $w \in \symcal{M}$ and $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$, $\symcal{M}, w \models \varphi$ if and only if $g_F(\symcal{M}), w \models \varphi$.
    \label{lem:closure-to-FMT-preserving}
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
By induction on the complexity of $\varphi$.
    The base case and the Boolean cases are straightforward.
    We only prove the case $\varphi = \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.

    Suppose first that $\symcal{M}, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi$. Then $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$. By the definition of $R^{g_F}_\psi$, there is no $v \in W$ such that $wR^{g_F}_\psi v$. Hence, $g_F(\symcal{M}), w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.

    Conversely, suppose that $\symcal{M}, w \nvDash \symbol{"25A1} \psi$. Then, $\psi \notin \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$. By the contrapositive of \textsf{(G)}, there is some $v \in W$ such that $\symcal{M}, v \nvDash \psi$. By the definition of $R^{g_F}_\psi$, we have $wR^{g_F}_\psi v$. Moreover, by the induction hypothesis, $\symcal{M}, v \nvDash \psi$ implies $g_F(\symcal{M}), v \nvDash \psi$. Therefore, $g_F(\symcal{M}), w \nvDash \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
The translations $f_F: \mathbf{FM} \to \mathbf{CM}_\mathsf{G}$ and $g_F: \mathbf{CM}_\mathsf{G} \to \mathbf{FM}$ are truth-preserving.
\label{thm:FMT-closure-representation}
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\[
        \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{FM}) = \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{CM_\mathsf{G}}).
    \]
    \label{cor:FMT-closure-equivalence}
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- definition-22: body_md -->
A \emph{Kripke frame} is a tuple $\symcal{F}_K= (W, R)$ where $W$ is a non-empty set and $R \subseteq W \times W$. A \emph{Kripke model} is a tuple $\symcal{M}_K = (W, R, V)$ where $(W, R)$ is a Kripke frame and $V$ is a valuation function $V: \symbf{Prop} \to \symcal{P}(W)$.
    The relation $\symcal{M}_K, w \models \varphi$ is defined in the usual way, and the modal operator is interpreted as follows:
    \[
        \symcal{M}_K, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \varphi
        \iff
        \text{for all } v \in W, \ w R v\text{ implies } \symcal{M}_K, v \models \varphi.
    \]
    \label{def:Kripke-model}
<!-- end definition-22 -->
<!-- definition-23: body_md -->
We say that a closure model $\symcal{M}=(W, G, \mathrm{cl}, V)$ has the property \textsf{(KRep)} if, for every $w\in W$ and $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$,
    \[
        \varphi\in\mathrm{cl}(G(w))
        \iff
        \bigcap_{\psi\in\mathrm{cl}(G(w))}\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}
        \subseteq
        \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}.
    \]
    \label{def:KRep}
<!-- end definition-23 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
Every closure model satisfying \textsf{(KRep)} satisfies both \textsf{(G)} and \textsf{(K)}.
    \label{lem:KRep-implies-GK}
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Suppose first that $\symcal{M}\models\varphi$. Then $\lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}=W$. Hence, for every $w\in W$,
    \[
        \bigcap_{\psi\in\mathrm{cl}(G(w))}\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}
        \subseteq
        W
        =
        \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}.
    \]
    By \textsf{(KRep)}, $\varphi\in\mathrm{cl}(G(w))$. Therefore, $\symcal{M}$ satisfies \textsf{(G)}.

    Next, suppose that $\varphi\to\psi\in\mathrm{cl}(G(w))$ and $\varphi\in\mathrm{cl}(G(w))$. Then
    \[
        \bigcap_{\chi\in\mathrm{cl}(G(w))}\lBrack \chi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}
        \subseteq
        \lBrack \varphi\to\psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}
        \cap
        \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}
        \subseteq
        \lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}.
    \]
    By \textsf{(KRep)}, $\psi\in\mathrm{cl}(G(w))$. Therefore, $\symcal{M}$ satisfies \textsf{(K)}.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
Let $\symcal{M} = (W, G, \mathrm{cl}, V)$ be a closure model where:
    \begin{align*}
        W &= \mathbb{N} \\
        G(w) &= \{ \varphi \mid W \setminus \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} \text{ is finite} \} \\
        \mathrm{cl} &= \mathrm{id} \\
        V(p_n) &= W \setminus \{n\} \text{ for all } n \in \mathbb{N},
        V(q) = \{ 2n \mid n \in \mathbb{N} \}.
    \end{align*}
    Note that this definition is well-founded, although $G$ is defined in terms of truth sets in $\symcal{M}$.
    Determining whether $\varphi \in G(w)$ requires only the truth set of $\varphi$, while this membership is used only to determine the truth value of the strictly more complex formula $\symbol{"25A1} \varphi$.
    
    This model satisfies $\textsf{(G)}$.
    If $\symcal{M} \models \varphi$, we have $\lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} = W$, which is equivalent to $W \setminus \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} = \emptyset$.
    Therefore, $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$.
    It also satisfies $\textsf{(K)}$. Suppose that $\varphi, \varphi \to \psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$. Then both $\lBrack \varphi\to\psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}$ and $\lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}$ have finite complements.
    Since $\lBrack \varphi\to\psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} \cap \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} \subseteq \lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}$, the set $\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}$ also has a finite complement. Therefore, $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$.

    On the other hand, $p_n \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, since $V(p_n)=W\setminus\{n\}$ is cofinite. Therefore,
    \[
        \bigcap_{\varphi\in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))}\lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}
        \subseteq
        \bigcap_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\lBrack p_n \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}
        =
        \emptyset.
    \]
    Since $\lBrack q \rBrack_{\symcal{M}} = \{ 2n \mid n \in \mathbb{N} \}$, we have
    \[
        \bigcap_{\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))} \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}
        \subseteq
        \lBrack q \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}.
    \]
    However, $q \notin G(w)$ because $W \setminus \lBrack q \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}$ is not finite. Therefore, the model does not satisfy \textsf{(KRep)}.
    \label{ex:GK-not-KRep}
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- definition-24: body_md -->
Given a Kripke model $\symcal{M}_K = (W, R, V)$, we define $f_K(\symcal{M}_K) = (W, G^{f_K}, \mathrm{id}, V)$ where
    \[
        G^{f_K}(w)
        =
        \{\varphi\in\mathbf{MF}\mid
        R[w]
        \subseteq
        \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_K}\}.
    \]
    \label{def:Kripke-to-closure-function}
<!-- end definition-24 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
Let $\symcal{M}_K$ be a Kripke model. Then, for any $w\in\symcal{M}_K$ and $\varphi\in\mathbf{MF}$, $\symcal{M}_K,w\models\varphi$ if and only if $f_K(\symcal{M}_K),w\models\varphi$.
    \label{lem:Kripke-to-closure-preserving}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
By induction on the complexity of $\varphi$. The base case and the Boolean cases are straightforward. We only prove the case $\varphi=\symbol{"25A1}\psi$ as follows:
    \begin{align*}
        \symcal{M}_K,w\models\symbol{"25A1}\psi
        &\iff (w R v \implies \symcal{M}_K, v \models \psi) \text{ for all } v \in \symcal{M}_K \\
        &\iff \psi\in G^{f_K}(w) \\
        &\iff \psi\in\mathrm{id}(G^{f_K}(w)) \\
        &\iff f_K(\symcal{M}_K),w\models\symbol{"25A1}\psi. \qedhere
    \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
For any Kripke model $\symcal{M}_K$, the closure model $f_K(\symcal{M}_K)$ has the property \textsf{(KRep)}.
    \label{lem:Kripke-has-KRep}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Let $w \in W$ and $\varphi \in \mathbf{MF}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:Kripke-to-closure-preserving}, the truth sets of formulas in $\symcal{M}_K$ and $f_K(\symcal{M}_K)$ coincide, i.e., we can freely use the fact that $\lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_K} = \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{f_K(\symcal{M}_K)}$ for any $\varphi$.

    The left-to-right direction is straightforward. For the converse direction, suppose that
    \[
        \bigcap_{\psi\in\mathrm{id}(G^{f_K}(w))} \lBrack \psi \rBrack_{f_K(\symcal{M}_K)} \subseteq \lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{f_K(\symcal{M}_K)} .
    \]
    For every $\psi\in G^{f_K}(w)$, we have $R[w]\subseteq\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_K}$. Hence,
    \[
        R[w]
        \subseteq
        \bigcap_{\psi\in G^{f_K}(w)}\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_K}
        =
        \bigcap_{\psi\in\mathrm{id}(G^{f_K}(w))}\lBrack \psi \rBrack_{f_K(\symcal{M}_K)}.
    \]
    Then, $R[w]\subseteq\lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}_K}$, and thus $\varphi\in G^{f_K}(w)=\mathrm{id}(G^{f_K}(w))$. Therefore, $f_K(\symcal{M}_K)$ satisfies \textsf{(KRep)}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- definition-25: body_md -->
Given a closure model $\symcal{M}=(W,G,\mathrm{cl},V)$, we define $g_K(\symcal{M})=(W,R^{g_K},V)$ where
    \[
        R^{g_K}[w]
        =        \bigcap_{\varphi\in\mathrm{cl}(G(w))}\lBrack \varphi \rBrack_{\symcal{M}}.
    \]
    \label{def:closure-to-Kripke-function}
<!-- end definition-25 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
Let $\symcal{M}$ be a closure model that satisfies \textsf{(KRep)}. Then, for any $w\in\symcal{M}$ and $\varphi\in\mathbf{MF}$, $\symcal{M},w\models\varphi$ if and only if $g_K(\symcal{M}),w\models\varphi$.
    \label{lem:closure-to-Kripke-preserving}
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
By induction on the complexity of $\varphi$. The base case and the Boolean cases are straightforward. We only prove the case $\varphi=\symbol{"25A1}\psi$.

    For the left-to-right direction, suppose $\symcal{M}, w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi$ and take an arbitrary $v$ such that $w R^{g_K} v$. From the former, $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$. From the definition of $R^{g_K}$, it follows that $\symcal{M}, v \models \psi$, which implies $g_K(\symcal{M}), v \models \psi$ by the induction hypothesis. Therefore, $g_K(\symcal{M}), w \models \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.

    The other direction is shown by using the contraposition. Suppose that $\symcal{M}, w \nvDash \symbol{"25A1} \psi$. Then, $\psi \notin \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$. From \textsf{(KRep)}, we have some $v \in \symcal{M}$ such that $\symcal{M}, v \models \chi$ for all $\chi \in \mathrm{cl}(G(w))$ and $\symcal{M}, v \nvDash \psi$. Take such $v$, and we have $w R^{g_K} v$ and $\symcal{M}, v \nvDash \psi$. From the latter together with the induction hypothesis, $g_K(\symcal{M}), v \nvDash \psi$ holds. Therefore, we have $g_K(\symcal{M}), w \nvDash \symbol{"25A1} \psi$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
The translations $f_K: \mathbf{KM} \to \mathbf{CM}_\mathsf{KRep}$ and $g_K: \mathbf{CM}_\mathsf{KRep} \to \mathbf{KM}$ are truth-preserving.
    \label{thm:Kripke-closure-representation}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\[
        \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{KM}) =
        \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{CM_\mathsf{KRep}}) = \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{CM_\mathsf{GK}}).
    \]
    \label{thm:Kripke-closure-equivalence}
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
The equality of the first two follows from the theorem above. By the soundness and completeness theorem for $L_{\mathsf{GK}}$ with respect to $\mathbf{CM_\mathsf{GK}}$ and Kripke models,  we have
    \[
        \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{CM_\mathsf{GK}})
        = \mathsf{Log}(\mathbf{KM})
        = L_{\mathsf{GK}}. \qedhere
    \]
<!-- end proof-26 -->
